text:
Elias Pettersson's name keeps coming up in the trade market chatter around Vancouver, but his season has been more interesting than the noise. He has 23 points in 23 games, 11 on the power play, and he's playing a far more physical game than his reputation: 40 hits and 32 blocked shots, enough that one outlet floated early Selke talk.

The scoring needs a closer look. Pettersson has only 27 shots on goal and 3.7 expected goals, and he's turned that into six goals on a 22% shooting rate. The Canucks have scored 9.8 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and at 5v5 they get just 42% of the expected goals with him out there. That's a team problem as much as his: Evolving-Hockey had him playing with teammates in the bottom 5% by impact last season, against top-10% competition.

His last ten games, 10 points against 9.8 expected, are exactly what the numbers say he is right now. Vancouver lost seven straight in that stretch before beating Vegas and Utah. That's the backdrop for every rumor.
headline: Pettersson's quiet, two-way season
